narrative.overview:
The portfolio is a public workbench: a calm, legible place where evidence, photographs, collective credit, and operating decisions have been sorted and made usable. Its visual language comes from working materials Jamie actually uses: a blue work jacket, correction marks, public records, meeting packets, index cards, and practical institutional forms.

The brand is the practice. The site should help a hiring reader see how Jamie turns emerging work into structure while preserving the people, limits, and sources that make each account trustworthy. Photography supplies presence and particularity. Type and layout supply the durable handoff.
keyCharacteristics: Dense enough to show real work, calm enough to scan.
Precise, warm, modular, and ethically grounded.
Evidence-led without resembling an archive browser.

rules.name: The Semantic Color Rule
rules.body: Color must clarify status, evidence, action, or reading hierarchy. If color only decorates, remove it.

rules.name: The Correction Rule
rules.body: Red marks accountable intervention, not generic urgency. Harm has its own darker red.

rules.name: The Ochre Rarity Rule
rules.body: Ochre earns attention through scarcity. Reserve it for focus, selection, disputed state, and occasional proof.

rules.name: The Plain Evidence Rule
rules.body: Use weight, spacing, and placement before visual effects. Letter spacing is zero except for the established label voice.

rules.name: The Scale Rule
rules.body: Hero-scale type belongs only in a hero. Dense professional surfaces use smaller, tighter headings.

rules.name: The Flat Workbench Rule
rules.body: Surfaces rest on the page. Lift appears only when it helps an actual object read as discrete.

rules.name: The Full-Border Rule
rules.body: Use a complete one-pixel boundary or none. Thick colored side stripes are forbidden.

dos: Do make the role, action, outcome, source basis, and honest limit scan quickly.
Do use photography to reveal real work, people, place, and participation.
Do preserve collective credit, consent, rights, attribution, and protected absence.
Do keep focus states, keyboard paths, reduced motion, and contrast at WCAG 2.2 AA or better.
Do keep public safety visible in case-study and photographic structures.
donts: Don't make the site feel like a generic SaaS landing page, a private archive browser, a consultant hype funnel, a heavy animated portfolio, or a decorative AI-generated template.

Don't publish inflated claims, unapproved metrics, raw transcripts, private coalition notes, legal-review materials, private correspondence, internal analytics, client-private material, unapproved photos, private fonts, or unapproved stakeholder details.
Don't use gradient text, glassmorphism, giant hero metrics, decorative side-stripe borders, repeated icon-card grids, or decorative background grids.
Don't make every section an uppercase eyebrow or numbered index.
Don't over-round cards or nest cards inside cards.
